previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent lower extremity cellulitis, chronic venous insufficiency, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for acute left leg pain, erythema, and swelling concerning for infection. Initial broad-spectrum antibiotics were given, later narrowed to cefazolin, then re-escalated to IV vancomycin due to worsening erythema. Dermatology and infectious disease confirmed cellulitis. During admission, she developed C. difficile colitis, requiring oral vancomycin. Blood cultures were negative, and ultrasound showed no abscess. She improved clinically, was transitioned to oral linezolid for completion of antibiotic therapy, and was discharged home with plans for infectious disease follow-up, warfarin monitoring, and resumption of home medications including torsemide once diarrhea resolved.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE
=====================
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with a significant PMHx of 
HTN, AS s/p ___ arrest s/p PPM, and recurrent ___ 
cellulitis complicated by severe C .diff infections, last 
treated 1 week prior to admission, who presented from home, with 
worsening bilateral ___ swelling and chronic ulcers with green, 
foul smelling drainage.

#Acute on Chronic HFpEF: On admission, the patient endorsed a 
20lbs weight gain over the past few weeks, along with subjective 
dyspnea and orthopnea X1 week. She had a +JVD with AJR, along 
with a BNP ~900. In addition, there was increased vascular 
congestion and cephalization on CXR. Etiologies for her 
exacerbation could include medication noncompliance, given that 
the patient stated she alternates between 20mg and 40mg of 
Torsemide. Further, the patient had purulent lower extremity 
ulcers and recent C diff infection, which could lead to an 
increased catecholamine response. The patient may also have a 
component of valvular disease, given her severe TR. There was no 
evidence for ischemia or arrhythmias as the EKG was unremarkable 
and she stated she complies with a strict low sodium diet. The 
patient clinically improved with IV diuresis with Lasix 100mg 
and 80mg IV. After a net negative of -9.5L since admission, the 
patient was at her dry weight. She was transitioned to PO 
Torsemide 40 mg daily and educated about the importance of 
strict medication adherence. 

#LLE cellulitis: The patient presented with healing ulcers, with 
minimal purulent drainage. Of note, she has a history of 
recurrent cellulitis previously treated with linezolid in 
___. In addition, she also has history of pseudomonas 
infections. Her preliminary wound culture was negative for PMNs 
and organisms. She was started on IV Vancomycin 1250mg Q12h on 
___ and transitioned to PO Linezolid at the time of 
discharge, to complete 14 days (___). Her erythema and edema 
improved considerably during her hospital stay. Of note, her 
LENIS were negative for DVT. 

#Paroxysmal A-fib: INR goal ___. Although the patient was 
subtherapeutic on admission to 1.9, she quickly came back to 
goal during the rest of her hospitalization. There was no 
evidence of acute bleeding. She was continued on fractionated 
metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily and home warfarin dosage(2 mg 
___, 3mg on ___.

WHAT HAPPENED AT THE HOSPITAL? 
===================================

legs. This was transitioned to an oral medication at discharge 
to take for a total of 14 days 
- You were also found to have fluid on your lungs. This was felt 
to be due to a condition called heart failure, where your heart 
does not pump hard enough and fluid backs up into your lungs. 
-You were given a diuretic medication through the IV to help get 
the fluid out. You improved considerably and were ready to leave 
the hospital.
-After continuing these medications for a few days, you felt 
much better and were discharged from the hospital on medications 
that you take by mouth.
